chapter: Fats Waller, marriage and Indian school tours
title: Pow Wows and playing for senior citizens
summary: Moore describes Pow Wow appearances and benefit concerts in Rockland County.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: What about in some of the Pow Wows, have you gone there and done any performing? When you go there do people recognize you as Big Chief Russell Moore that the jazz world knows or do you blend in with anyone else and you're just sort of a spectator and a member of the big family that is part of the Pow Wow scene?
Well, yes, when I was on those school tours I didn't have time to go to any Pow Wows, you know. But I've attended some Pow Wows, especially
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

Yes, everybody seemed to know me and the Master of Ceremonies at the dances-they'd always introduce me and I'd go up and say a few words and sing one of my Pima chants, and it's beautiful to be recognized. It's nice, good feeling. And you try to reciprocate by performing. Even now, around my neighborhood here in Rockland County I do things for senior citizens. I do benefits just to keep in trim and my chops in line right here and I'm semi-retired, but I still love to go out and play now. Next Wednesday I will be playing in an Armstrong program of tunes along with the piano player and Miss Ann Price who is the choir director of the New City Methodist Church is going to accompany me with the music and I'm going to sing it, play my horn and I don't get a cent for that. I'm glad to do it because it keeps me in trim and people like to hear me and I always get a good reception.

One of the funny things that happened the last time I did one, now these are all senior citizens, some of them are sitting in wheelchairs, some are sitting in rocking chairs -- I announced the next number. I'm going to play and sing a number that I
